summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag, a Slack-based agentic teammate that can be tagged by any team member to plan and execute delegated tasks, replacing the existing Claude in Slack app.

mechanisms.reason: Anthropic states its own product team already has agents producing the majority of its code and delegates work to many parallel agents, illustrating a shift from seat-based work to agent-executed tasks.
mechanisms.quote: Today, 65% of our product team’s code is created by our internal version of Claude Tag.

mechanisms.reason: Delegating tasks to many parallel, asynchronous agents that plan multi-stage work implies more model calls issued per task.
mechanisms.quote: we now spend much more of our time delegating tasks to many Claudes in parallel.

practices.reason: The described pattern of task decomposition, persistent cross-channel memory, ambient proactivity and async scheduling is a scaffolding design worth evaluating, though it is Anthropic's own hosted implementation rather than a transferable recipe.
practices.quote: Tag @Claude with a request in simple terms and it’ll break its task down into stages and then work through them in turn, using the tools it has access to.

practices.reason: Existing Claude-in-Slack integrations must be migrated to the new Claude Tag app within a defined window, which is scheduled integration work for any team using the old app.
practices.quote: Claude Tag replaces the existing Claude in Slack app. To migrate, administrators can opt in within 30 days.

notable_reason: The disclosed internal metric that 65% of Anthropic's own product code is now generated via agentic Slack delegation is a concrete, quantified data point on agentic workflow adoption that sector watchers would want to see.
